parts.label: Part 4
parts.article:
Hello everyone. I recently completed some important research into the way office space is designed and its impact on employees. The open plan office has been the norm for offices around the world, I'm sure you can picture one. A big room with maybe 50 or 100 workers sitting at their workstations.
You might think open plan designs are a recent phenomenon but they actually came about in the early 20th century when businesses needed large numbers of people to do typing. These employees, usually women, used to have to sit in rows working away at their typewriters under the watchful eye of their supervisor.
Over the years designers have come up with several variations on the open theme. In particular, this has been achieved through furnishings. The early designs featured separate desks. A subsequent design introduced the concept of the cubicle. These can have either high screens that workers can't see over or a screen just low enough to keep a lookout for the manager. And nowadays, with the increase in large call centres, a phenomenon known as hot desking is common. In this system, employees working on different shifts are asked to share the same workstation. As you can imagine, this is not very popular with staff as there is little opportunity to personalise your workspace.
In fact, my research shows that employees in general dislike the open plan design. As a part of my research, I conducted a survey of the staff in several large companies with open plan offices. The employees all voiced similar concerns about the design. Firstly, they felt that the open plan took away their privacy but many also felt the need to carry their valuables with them at all times. So, to some extent, they also felt there was less security with these designs. Another common complaint may be something for employers to consider when choosing this type of design. And this was that these types of office space are bad for the health. I was intrigued by this possibility, but looking at staff records, it does seem to be borne out.
So, if this design is so unpopular, why is it so commonplace? Well, the answer to that is in the benefits that the employers feel this type of design has. Of course, there is the obvious benefit that this design significantly reduces costs, both in terms of rent and even in terms of energy use. Employers also argue that an open plan design leads to better teamwork and communication. They also feel that new staff can learn from observing other workers, so this design can actually help in training staff.
However, the complaints voiced by employees seem to suggest that the disadvantages far outweigh the advantages. The reality is that unhappy workers are unlikely to work well together, and there is plenty of evidence to suggest workers are frequently distracted from their work by the noise that is all around them. What is clear is that as designers, we need to think carefully about the impact that our design has both on the staff involved and the work that they do.

analyses.content: 录音提到企业需要大量人员来“打字”，这些人通常被安排成排坐着。

You might think open plan designs are a recent phenomenon but they actually came about in the early 20th century when businesses needed large numbers of people to do typing. These employees, usually women, used to have to sit in rows working away at their typewriters under the watchful eye of their supervisor.
听到 typewriters（打字机）时别急着填，题目空格前是 do，后面需要接一个动作或任务名称，typing 才是正确答案。
Over the years designers have come up with several variations on the open theme. In particular, this has been achieved through furnishings. The early designs featured separate desks.
题目中的 individual（个人的）对应录音中的 separate（分开的），注意不要填成 broad term 如 furnishings（家具）。
录音中说早期的设计主要通过陈设来实现，具体特征是拥有独立的“桌子”。
A subsequent design introduced the concept of the cubicle. These can have either high screens that workers can't see over or a screen just low enough to keep a lookout for the manager.
这里的 high or low 是形容词，紧跟其后的名词 screens 是核心答案，不要被 cubicle（格子间）这个大概念干扰。
录音描述了后来的格子间设计，它们拥有高或低的“屏风/隔板”。
And nowadays, with the increase in large call centres, a phenomenon known as hot desking is common. In this system, employees working on different shifts are asked to share the same workstation.
题目空格前是 have to，需要填一个动词原形，hot desking 是这种现象的名词，不要填错了。
录音提到现在的轮用办公桌现象中，不同班次的员工被要求“共享”同一个工作站。

As a part of my research, I conducted a survey of the staff in several large companies with open plan offices. The employees all voiced similar concerns about the design. Firstly, they felt that the open plan took away their privacy but many also felt the need to carry their valuables with them at all times.
题目中的 lack of（缺乏）对应录音中的 took away（带走/剥夺），直接填入 privacy 即可。
录音中的调查显示，员工首先觉得开放式设计剥夺了他们的“隐私”。
录音接着提到，员工觉得在这种设计下“安全感”降低了，需要随身携带贵重物品。

Firstly, they felt that the open plan took away their privacy but many also felt the need to carry their valuables with them at all times. So, to some extent, they also felt there was less security with these designs.
不要填 valuables（贵重物品），这是因为缺乏 security 才导致需要携带的东西，不是缺乏的东西本身。

Another common complaint may be something for employers to consider when choosing this type of design. And this was that these types of office space are bad for the health. I was intrigued by this possibility, but looking at staff records, it does seem to be borne out.
题目 pose a risk to（对...构成风险）对应录音中的 bad for（对...有害），不要填 staff records，那是证据。
录音指出这类办公空间对“健康”有害，且员工记录也证实了这一点。
Of course, there is the obvious benefit that this design significantly reduces costs, both in terms of rent and even in terms of energy use.
题目中 rent 和空格是并列关系，共同修饰 costs，录音中明确说了 rent and energy use，填 energy 最符合语境。
雇主认为开放式设计能降低租金和“能源”使用的成本。

Employers also argue that an open plan design leads to better teamwork and communication. They also feel that new staff can learn from observing other workers, so this design can actually help in training staff.
题目 make ... easier 对应录音中的 help in，不要填 observing，那是手段，training 才是目的。
录音提到新员工可以通过观察他人来学习，因此这种设计有助于“培训”员工。

The reality is that unhappy workers are unlikely to work well together, and there is plenty of evidence to suggest workers are frequently distracted from their work by the noise that is all around them.
听到 distracted from their work by... 时，紧接着的 noise 就是答案，不要被前面的 unhappy workers 干扰。
录音最后总结，员工经常被周围的“噪音”分心，导致无法协同工作。
